headline: Traffic decline drags margins and profit lower
summary_short: Wendy's Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended March 29, 2026) revenue rose 3.3% y/y to $540.6M, but global same-restaurant sales fell 6.8% on lower traffic, compressing Company-operated restaurant margin 350bp to 10.8% and driving diluted EPS down 36.8% y/y to $0.12.
summary_long: Revenue rose 3.3% y/y to $540.6M on the 2025 franchise-restaurant acquisition and higher franchise fees, but global same-restaurant sales fell 6.8% (U.S. -7.8%) on lower traffic, partly offset by higher average check. Company-operated margin compressed 350bp to 10.8% on higher cost of sales and G&A, up $4.6M on compensation and professional fees. Operating income fell 21.9% y/y to $64.9M and EBITDA fell 10.6% to $113.6M as U.S. segment weakness outweighed International and Real Estate gains. Pretax income fell 37.8% to $34.2M, driving net income down 42.1% to $22.7M and diluted EPS down 36.8% to $0.12. No buybacks this quarter; dividend held at $0.14/share. Cash was $298.7M. No guidance issued in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Global same-restaurant sales fell 6.8% (U.S. -7.8%, International -0.4%) on lower traffic partly offset by higher average check; Company-operated restaurant margin fell 350bp to 10.8% and income before income taxes fell 37.8% to $34.2 million.

U.S. revenue growth was primarily due to the Q3-2025 acquisition of 35 franchise-operated restaurants, higher franchise fees, higher advertising fund revenue and net new restaurant development, partially offset by the same-restaurant sales decline.

U.S. and Global Company-operated restaurant margin compressed (U.S. to 11.4% from 14.8%, Global to 10.8% from 14.3%) on higher cost of sales as a percent of sales, driven by the same-restaurant sales decline.

Wendy's U.S. segment profit fell $11.1M primarily on higher cost of sales (percent of sales) and higher franchise support costs, partly offset by higher revenue; G&A also rose $4.6M on employee compensation and professional fees.
Wendy's U.S. segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $109.9M from $121.0M, outweighing gains in Wendy's International ($10.6M from $9.4M) and Global Real Estate & Development ($28.1M from $24.7M).
Net income decline tracks the 37.8% drop in pretax income from lower segment profit and higher G&A; the filing does not separately break out a change in effective tax rate as a driver.
Diluted EPS fell to $0.12 from $0.19, tracking the 42.1% net income decline, only partly cushioned by a lower diluted share count (190.9M vs 201.6M) from prior-year buybacks.
